title: Medical Diagnosis Assistant
description: An AI assistant that drafts possible diagnoses and care suggestions from patient notes.
business_goal: Reduce the time doctors spend on documentation and offer second opinions on complex cases.
users: Hospital clinicians (about 150 licensed physicians and nurses).

architecture.name: Clinicians
architecture.purpose: Physicians and nurses enter patient notes and review suggested diagnoses.
security_considerations: Clinicians have broad legitimate access to health records
Mobile devices are used at the bedside
architecture.attack_surface: A lost or stolen clinician session exposes protected health data.

architecture.name: Clinical Web App
architecture.purpose: Secure portal where the assistant is integrated into the clinical workflow.
security_considerations: Must comply with health data protection rules
architecture.attack_surface: Weak session handling exposes patient records.

architecture.name: AI Gateway
architecture.purpose: Routes clinical prompts to the model and is supposed to filter protected health data.
security_considerations: Filtering is configured broadly and often bypassed
No approval step before the model
architecture.attack_surface: Health data passes to the model without a governance decision.

architecture.name: Clinical LLM
architecture.purpose: Model trained on clinical text that drafts possible diagnoses.
security_considerations: Diagnoses are suggestions, not medical advice
architecture.attack_surface: Patient data in prompts is retained by a third party.

architecture.name: Knowledge Store
architecture.purpose: Retrieves relevant clinical guidelines and similar historical cases.
security_considerations: Similar cases may contain patient identifiers
architecture.attack_surface: Retrieved patient data leaks into the generated answer.

architecture.name: Medical Records
architecture.purpose: Source electronic health records that populate the assistant context.
security_considerations: Access should be on a need-to-know basis
architecture.attack_surface: Every record retrieved is a disclosure of protected health information.

architecture.name: Audit Logging
architecture.purpose: Records which clinician asked which question and what the model replied.
architecture.attack_surface: Logs become a second copy of protected health data.

architecture.name: Safety Monitoring
architecture.purpose: Watch for unsafe suggestions and model drift.
architecture.attack_surface: A dangerous suggestion can reach a clinician before any review.

threats.name: Protected health data to a third party
threats.description: Full patient notes are sent to a hosted model provider without a governance decision.
threats.business_consequences: Severe regulatory breach, fines, and a loss of patient trust that is hard to rebuild.

threats.name: Unsafe diagnosis suggestion
threats.description: The model states a confident but wrong diagnosis that a clinician may follow.
threats.business_consequences: Patient harm, liability, and an immediate loss of clinical trust.

threats.name: Biased care suggestions
threats.description: The model treats some patient groups differently because of training data bias.
threats.business_consequences: Unequal care and potential discrimination claims.

threats.name: Wide record access
threats.description: Any clinician can retrieve records for patients outside their care team.
threats.business_consequences: Protected health data is seen by staff with no clinical need.

threats.name: Instructions hidden in notes
threats.description: Text inside a patient note instructs the model to change its behavior or expose data.
threats.business_consequences: Model behavior is hijacked inside a clinical context.

threats.name: Corrupted fine-tuning data
threats.description: The model is fine-tuned on clinical text that includes poisoned or incorrect labels.
threats.business_consequences: Systematic wrong suggestions across many patients.

threats.name: Records in audit logs
threats.description: Prompts and replies containing patient data are stored in logs with broad access.
threats.business_consequences: A second uncontrolled copy of protected health data.

teaching_points: Health data has the highest stakes: the risk is patient harm, not only a fine.
Hallucination in a clinical tool is a safety failure, so output validation matters most.
Retrieval of similar cases can leak identifiers even when the question is clean.
Human approval is essential before a suggestion becomes a decision.
